Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric target-board rings on older foliage, surrounded by chlorotic yellow halos.
Tomato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) combined with high humidity, heavy dew, or overhead irrigation.
Tomato___Early_blight.severity: High (Yield loss up to 50-70% if unmanaged)
Tomato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil (0.2%), Mancozeb (0.25%), or Azoxystrobin at 7-10 day intervals upon first appearance.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Foliar application of Copper octanoate (copper soap) or Bacillus subtilis (Serenade). Weekly neem oil (0.5%) emulsion.
Tomato___Early_blight.cultural_prevention: Stake plants for air circulation, avoid overhead sprinkler watering, practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops, and mulch base.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly expanding water-soaked dark olive to black lesions with pale green borders; white fuzzy sporulation under leaf surface in humid conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Cool, moist weather (15-22°C) with persistent leaf wetness and relative humidity >90%.
Tomato___Late_blight.severity: Critical (Total crop destruction possible within 7-14 days)
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Systemic fungicides: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold 2g/L), Cymoxanil, or Dimethomorph.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_remedy: Fixed copper fungicides (Bordeaux mixture 1%) applied protectively before rain events.
Tomato___Late_blight.cultural_prevention: Destroy infected volunteer plants, ensure wide row spacing, use certified disease-free transplants, and install drip irrigation.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe upward leaf cupping, curling, interveinal chlorosis (yellowing), marked leaf reduction, and stunted bush growth with flower drop.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.favorable_conditions: Warm climates favoring high populations of the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.severity: High (Causes near 100% loss if infection occurs before flowering)
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_treatment: No direct cure for viral infection. Vector control: Imidacloprid (0.3ml/L), Thiamethoxam, or Acetamiprid to suppress whiteflies.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_remedy: Yellow sticky traps (20-25 traps/acre), insecticidal potassium soap spray, and neem kernel extract (5%).
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cultural_prevention: Install 50-mesh insect-proof netting in greenhouses, remove infected plants immediately, and plant TYLCV-resistant varieties.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green coloration, well-defined venation, firm turgid foliage, and no necrotic lesions or chlorosis.
Tomato___healthy.favorable_conditions: Optimum sunlight (6-8 hours daily), balanced N-P-K (10-10-10) fertilization, and soil pH 6.2-6.8.
Tomato___healthy.chemical_treatment: No chemical intervention needed. Maintain routine agronomic monitoring.
Tomato___healthy.organic_remedy: Prophylactic compost tea and seaweed extract foliar spray for boosted plant immunity.
Tomato___healthy.cultural_prevention: Standard crop management, consistent watering, and regular scouting.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown, angular target-board lesions delimited by major veins, with yellow chlorotic halos on lower mature leaflets.
Potato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Alternating wet and dry periods, warm temperatures (22-30°C), and stressed crop canopy.
Potato___Early_blight.severity: Moderate to High (Premature defoliation and tuber size reduction)
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L), Propineb, or Difenoconazole (0.5ml/L) at tuber initiation.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Copper hydroxide spray and Trichoderma viride biological antagonist soil application.
Potato___Early_blight.cultural_prevention: Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium fertility; avoid sprinkler irrigation late in the afternoon.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale-to-dark brown spots near leaf margins, rapidly coalescing into black dead tissue with white mildew.
Potato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Temperatures 10-20°C with relative humidity above 90% for prolonged intervals.
Potato___Late_blight.severity: Devastating (Historical cause of the Great Irish Famine; rapid total loss)
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Preventative: Mancozeb (2.5g/L). Curative: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (Curzate 2g/L) or Fenamidone.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_remedy: Bordeaux mixture (1%) protective coverage; harvest haulm destruction before lifting tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.cultural_prevention: Plant certified seed tubers, hill potatoes well to protect tubers, and eliminate cull piles.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Lush vibrant emerald leaflets, smooth margin texture, robust vein structural integrity, no spot deformities.
Potato___healthy.favorable_conditions: Cool season conditions (15-20°C), deep loose well-drained loamy soil, balanced irrigation.
Potato___healthy.cultural_prevention: Proper hilling, weed suppression, balanced nitrogen management.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Elongated golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered abundantly on both upper and lower leaf surfaces; ruptures epidermis with powdery spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures (16-25°C) and high relative humidity (>95%).
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.severity: Moderate (Yield reduction of 10-25% in susceptible grain hybrids)
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical_treatment: Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (Amistar Top 1ml/L) or Pyraclostrobin at first tassel emergence.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_remedy: Sulfur dusting (80% WP) or biological treatment with Ampelomyces quisqualis hyperparasite.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cultural_prevention: Select rust-resistant hybrids (Rp single-gene resistance), early planting to escape late spore showers.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5-15 cm long) with distinctive tapered ends, parallel to leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C) accompanied by extended periods of heavy dew.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.severity: High (Severe defoliation leading to grain fill failure and stalk rot)
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L), Mancozeb, or Pyraclostrobin applied at VT-R1 growth stages.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_remedy: Bio-fungicide sprays containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens and silicon-based foliar enhancers.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cultural_prevention: Tillage to bury residue, 2-year crop rotation with soybeans, and deployment of Ht-gene resistant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Broad, elongated ribbon-like blade with prominent central whitish-green midrib; rich uniform chlorophyll density.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.favorable_conditions: Full sun, warm temperatures (21-32°C), consistent soil moisture during vegetative growth.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.organic_remedy: Foliar zinc and boron micronutrient supplementation.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.cultural_prevention: Optimal planting density (65,000-75,000 plants/ha) and weed canopy control.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dull velvety black circular lesions with feathery margins; leaf tissue distorts, curls, and drops prematurely.
Apple___Apple_scab.favorable_conditions: Spring wetness periods (Mills infection table) with temperatures between 13-24°C.
Apple___Apple_scab.severity: High (Fruit deformities and up to 70% unmarketable crop)
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_treatment: Captan 50 WP (2.5g/L), Difenoconazole, Myclobutanil, or Dodine timed around rain events.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_remedy: Lime sulfur or wettable sulfur applied pre-bloom; potassium bicarbonate spray.
Apple___Apple_scab.cultural_prevention: Rake and shred fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate pseudothecia overwintering.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots developing into 'frog-eye' lesions with tan centres and dark purple-brown concentric borders.
Apple___Black_rot.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (26-28°C) following rainy periods during bloom and early petal fall.
Apple___Black_rot.severity: Moderate to Severe (Branch cankers, leaf defoliation, and mummified black fruit)
Apple___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Thiophanate-methyl, Captan, or Strobilurin fungicides applied from pink bud stage.
Apple___Black_rot.organic_remedy: Liquid copper applied at bud break; bio-protective Bacillus subtilis strains.
Apple___Black_rot.cultural_prevention: Prune out dead wood, mummified fruits, and fire blight cankers which harbor spores.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Glossy ovate foliage, finely serrated margin, vivid chlorophyll saturation without blemishes.
Apple___healthy.favorable_conditions: Chilling requirement met in winter, 6-8 hrs full sunlight, well-aerated loam soil.
Apple___healthy.organic_remedy: Foliar kelp extract and calcium nitrate sprays for cell wall strengthening.
Apple___healthy.cultural_prevention: Annual dormant pruning for sunlight penetration and canopy aeration.

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular blistering spots on leaf undersides, becoming dark brown with greasy texture and pale yellow halos.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.favorable_conditions: High temperatures (24-30°C) with frequent rainfall, overhead irrigation, and wind-driven rain.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.severity: High (Severe leaf drop exposes fruit to sunscald; significant yield collapse)
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide (Kocide 2g/L) tank-mixed with Mancozeb (to combat copper-resistant bacterial strains).
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_remedy: Bacteriophage treatments (AgriPhage), Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, and potassium silicate.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.cultural_prevention: Use hot water treated seeds (50°C for 25 min), avoid working in wet foliage, and rotate away from solanaceous crops for 2 years.

Pepper__bell___healthy.symptoms: Smooth, lanceolate to ovate leaf blade with unbroken glossy cuticle, vibrant green color, strong petiolar connection.
Pepper__bell___healthy.favorable_conditions: Warm growing season (21-28°C), steady drip moisture, magnesium and calcium supplemented soil.
Pepper__bell___healthy.organic_remedy: Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) foliar spray for enhanced chlorophyll synthesis.
Pepper__bell___healthy.cultural_prevention: Plastic mulch, drip fertigation, and regular scouting.
